First Nations business support should be designed and delivered by First Nations-led organisations.
Grants should be able to fund core operating costs, not only short projects.
Procurement programs should be measured by contracts won and paid, not supplier registrations alone.
Governments and large organisations should publish their actual spend with First Nations-owned businesses.
Large buyers should use shorter payment terms for small First Nations businesses.
Founders should be able to choose mentors with relevant industry and growth experience.
Regional and remote founders should be able to access programs without mandatory travel.
Founders should be paid for substantial consultation and advisory work.
First Nations founders should retain control of their intellectual property and cultural knowledge.
Business programs should include practical cybersecurity and data-protection support.
Complex grant and procurement applications exclude otherwise capable founders.
Peer and wellbeing support should be part of business-growth programs.
Investors and funding panels should disclose who makes decisions and how conflicts are managed.
Business success should include community benefit, not revenue and job numbers alone.
Programs should publish eligibility rules, assessment criteria and aggregate outcomes.
